background_notes.fact: A compact C0⊂X is closed and Lebesgue measurable. For real a≤b, [a,b] is compact, and C0×[a,b] is compact in Z. The half-space Ω={r>0} is open.

grounds.reason: X is finite-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard Lebesgue measure.
Z has the product norm topology.

background_notes.justification: Closed bounded real intervals are compact; finite products of compact spaces are compact. Compact subsets of a Hausdorff Euclidean space are closed, hence Borel and Lebesgue measurable. The continuous time projection pulls back the open interval (0,∞) to Ω. The displayed endpoint inequalities place the product inside Ω.

background_notes.fact: If f:Z→V is Fréchet differentiable at z with derivative L, then ‖f‖² is Fréchet differentiable there with derivative h↦2⟪f(z),Lh⟫; the affine curve c(s)=(x,s) has derivative τ.

grounds.reason: A001/A002 give differentiability of the actual vector fields at z=(x,r), r>0; S003 explicitly gives the remainder expansion.
V is a real Euclidean inner product space.

background_notes.justification: Write f(z+h)=f(z)+Lh+ρ(h) with ‖ρ(h)‖=o(‖h‖). Expanding the square leaves the continuous linear term 2⟪f(z),Lh⟫ and remainder 2⟪f(z),ρ(h)⟫+‖Lh+ρ(h)‖²=o(‖h‖), by boundedness of L and the inner-product estimate. For c, the increment is exactly hτ. These verify the derivative premises used by E013 and supplement the displayed local argument.

background_notes.fact: An ordinary real derivative at a point is unique. A smooth function on an open set is continuous there; restriction to a subset and pullback along a continuous spatial-section map preserve continuity.

grounds.reason: E015 and E013 give two ordinary derivatives, respectively Gdens(r)(x) and e_t(x,r), of the same total section s↦e(x,s).
N002 supplies smoothness of e_t,T,A_j at positive times.
K0⊂Ω and all times used are positive.

background_notes.justification: Each ordinary derivative equals the limit of the same difference quotient, whose limit is unique in ℝ. Differentiability implies continuity by the linear-remainder representation; smoothness supplies local differentiability. Continuous restrictions and compositions follow directly from inverse images of open sets. Thus the identified Gdens field is continuous on Ω and on K0.

background_notes.fact: For a real Bochner-integrable function on X, a.e. strong measurability holds. At a fixed positive time, constant multiples and finite sums of the supplied continuous sections are continuous; if every section vanishes off C0, so do these combinations.

grounds.reason: N002 explicitly supplies integrability, continuity and common support of e,e_t,T,A_j at the times under consideration.
I0 lies in the interval of the common-support assertion.

background_notes.justification: A.e. strong measurability is a constituent of Bochner integrability. Continuity of multiplication by a fixed real scalar and addition gives continuity of the finite combinations. At x∉C0 every term is zero, so the combination is zero. This justifies both measurability premises of E001 and the exact zero-extension identifications in A014.

background_notes.fact: At t0>0, changing total representatives only at nonpositive times leaves the ordinary derivative of E at t0 and the positive-time Fréchet derivative fields unchanged.

background_notes.justification: Two total representatives agreeing on Ω agree on a neighborhood of each positive-time point, so their Fréchet derivatives and iterated derivative fields agree there by the defining local limits. Their density integrals agree throughout I0. Difference quotients at t0 consequently coincide for all sufficiently small increments, giving identical ordinary derivatives.
